question.question:
A mine is bought at the start of Year 1 for 900000 USD; land residual value 175000 USD is recoverable after extraction. Initial ore estimate: 700000 units. Rate per unit = carrying amount minus residual value, divided by estimated remaining units when set; yearly depletion = units extracted times the rate in force. Extraction is 110000 units in each of Years 1 and 2. At the start of Year 3 (before extraction) remaining ore is re-estimated at 400000 units, replacing the earlier one; a new rate is set prospectively from the carrying amount then, with no restatement of prior years. Year 3 extraction is 50000 units. After Year 3 depletion, a one-time development cost of 250000 USD is capitalized at end of Year 3 (no residual, not recurring). At the start of Year 4 the rate is reset from the carrying amount then and remaining units of 400000 minus Year 3 extraction. Year 4 extraction is 330000 units; if it exceeds remaining estimated units, depletion is charged only on the remaining units. Carrying amount = total capitalized cost minus accumulated depletion since acquisition. Find the Year 3 rate per unit, Year 3 depletion, end-of-Year-4 accumulated depletion and carrying amount, and Year 4 depletion.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

Depletion expense recorded for Year 3
Accumulated depletion at end of Year 4 covering all four years
Carrying amount at end of Year 4 after development cost and depletion
